title: Anansi and Turtle Share a Meal
text:
Anansi the spider had just cooked a delicious pot of yams when Turtle arrived at his door, tired and hungry after a long walk. In Ashanti custom a visitor at mealtime must be fed, so Anansi had to invite him in. But he had no intention of sharing.

As Turtle reached for the food, Anansi stopped him. "Turtle, your hands are filthy from the road. Go to the river and wash them first." Turtle went down to the river and washed, but the path back was dusty, and since he walked on his hands, they were dirty again when he arrived. Anansi sent him back to wash a second time. When Turtle finally returned, walking on the grass to keep clean, the pot was empty. Anansi had eaten everything. Turtle said nothing but invited Anansi to dine at his home some day.

When Anansi came, Turtle's home was at the bottom of the river. Turtle swam down and began to eat. Anansi tried to dive but kept floating to the surface, so he filled the pockets of his jacket with stones and sank to the table.

Just as he reached for the food, Turtle said politely, "In my house we do not wear jackets at the table." Anansi took off his jacket, shot up to the surface, and watched from above as Turtle finished the meal.
lesson: If you treat a guest or partner unfairly through some clever rule, expect the same rules to be used on you. Generosity is cheaper than cleverness in the long run.
source: Ashanti (Akan) folk tradition of Anansi tales
